success_patterns: Every success had passages that restated the clue almost word for word (Kon-Tiki 101 days, jicama 'Mexican potato', Yoruba '21 percent', boomerang 'sickle-shaped', bumpkin 'little barrel', Swiss cheese 'Americans refer to', Ace 'place with the helpful hardware folks'). The agent took the entity that repeatedly sat next to the clue's key phrase.

For definition, etymology, synonym or alias clues (bumpkin, boomerang, jicama, Swiss cheese), the agent answered with the headword or alternate name the dictionary or reference snippets define. It did not answer with a word from inside the definition.

The agent kept a generic word when it belongs to the standard name ('Swiss cheese', 'Ace Hardware'). It used the plural when the clue said 'these' ('Crabs'). It gave a bare, short answer with no explanation.
When a J! Archive or GitHub-dump line contained the clue (Crabs. right: Amy; Ace Hardware; bumpkin), the agent copied the archived answer.

patch.reasoning: Most observed successes follow behaviors the skill already covers (verbatim clue match, answer the referent, short exact-match form). Two compact reinforcements remain. (1) Definition, etymology and alias clues: answer with the headword or alternate name that reference snippets give for the clue's key phrase. This was only proposed inside a larger rejected bundle, so it is restated here in a minimal form. (2) A balance for the 'drop descriptor words' rule: keep a generic noun when it is part of the standard name, as in 'Swiss cheese'. Both are short, so they should not dilute the document.

edits.target: - Otherwise, build the answer from passages that match several of the clue's details.
edits.content: - Definition, etymology, synonym and alias clues ('From the Middle Dutch for "little barrel", it's another way of saying yokel', 'Americans refer to Emmentaler as this', 'sickle-shaped weapon of the Aborigines'): find the dictionary or reference snippet that restates the clue's key phrase and answer with the term it defines (the headword, e.g. 'bumpkin', 'Boomerang') or the alternate name it gives ('Swiss cheese'). Do not answer with a word from inside the definition (yokel, hayseed, sickle).

edits.target: - Use the shortest standard form that names the entity, as a trivia answer key would.
edits.content: Keep a generic word when it is part of the entity's standard name or when the passages pair it with the clue's anchor ('Swiss cheese', 'Ace Hardware'). Drop role or descriptor words only when they are not part of that name.
